# API reference

:::caution[v3 release candidate, unreleased]

This is the reference for `@obolnetwork/obol-sdk@3.0.0-rc.12`, generated from its source and spec. Names and shapes may still change before 3.0.0, and it is not on npm `latest`. For the released SDK see the [2.x reference](../../sdk/index.md).

:::

Generated from the SDK source (signatures, TSDoc, types) and its spec (checks, error codes, findings). Grouped as the client exposes it: `obol.<namespace>.<method>`.

<div class="sdk-table">

| Namespace | Lifecycle | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| [Client and chains](./client.md) | Set up the client | One client binds every module to one chain, a viem `PublicClient`, an optional `WalletClient` (for EIP-712 signatures and `send`) and the Obol API (or `api: false` for chain-only). |
| [obol.terms](./terms.md) | Set up the client | The Obol terms and conditions must be accepted once per address before it can create a cluster definition or accept an invite. |
| [obol.setup](./setup.md) | Withdrawal and reward contracts | Deploys an Obol Validator Manager (OVM) and the SplitV2 splits behind its principal and reward recipients, in one transaction where possible. |
| [obol.cluster](./cluster.md) | Create and join the cluster | Cluster definitions and locks: build and post a definition, accept it as an operator, follow it until the lock is published, and verify definitions and locks (hashes, EIP-712 and EIP-1271 signatures, BLS share binding and deposit signatures) without running Charon. |
| [obol.deposits](./deposits.md) | Deposit | Turns a verified lock into deposits and sends them safely: `fromLock` verifies the lock and returns the deposit data for one amount, `status` reads what the beacon chain already has for each pubkey (Obol API with EIP-6110 pending deposits, or a beacon node), and `prepareDeposit` checks credentials, signatures, OVM provenance and roles, and that a new validator does not exist yet, before building the batch or OVM deposit transactions. |
| [obol.ovm](./ovm.md) | Operate | Reads and writes for an Obol Validator Manager: where a contract came from (`getProvenance`), its state, roles and validators, EIP-7002 withdrawal and exit requests, EIP-7251 consolidations, distributions, and the role and ownership writes. |
| [obol.splits](./splits.md) | Distribute and claim | SplitV2 splits: share math in parts per million (`percent`, `splitParams`), deterministic addresses (`predictSplit`), creation, reads, and `prepareDistributeAll`, which distributes an OVM, the splits behind its recipients and the recipients' Warehouse balances in one transaction. |
| [obol.incentives](./incentives.md) | Distribute and claim | Obol incentives paid in OBOL through Merkle distributors: read what an address can claim, run every claim check without sending (`preflight`), and prepare the claim. |
| [obol.exits](./exits.md) | Exit, withdraw, consolidate | Charon partial exits as the Obol API stores them: `assertPartialExit` runs the checks the API runs before storing an operator's partial exit signatures, and `aggregate` combines a threshold of them into a signed voluntary exit (EIP-7044 domain, mainnet and Hoodi). |
| [obol.withdrawals](./withdrawals.md) | Exit, withdraw, consolidate | EIP-7002 withdrawal and exit requests for a validator whose withdrawal credentials point at an EOA, sent by that address straight to the predeploy. |
| [send and acknowledgements](./send.md) | every stage | `send` is the one place a transaction leaves the SDK. |
| [obol.experimental](./experimental.md) | every stage | Features whose result shapes may still change in a minor release. |
| [Standalone checks](./checks.md) | DKG and lock | Root exports that need no client, for servers that verify what users send them (the Obol API uses them): `isValidLock` (a boolean; [`cluster.verifyLock`](./cluster.md#verifyLock) returns the failing step), `isValidTypedDataSignature` (an EIP-712 bearer signature from an account or, through EIP-1271, a Safe), and the error helpers. |
| [@obolnetwork/obol-sdk/blst](./blst.md) | DKG and lock | Node-only entry with the native BLS backend over the optional peer dependency `@chainsafe/blst`. |

</div>
